candidate.flaw_one_line: With the default cookie store, a Cookie header the caller set directly is replaced by the store's cookies, so in a multi-user application one user's request can go out with another user's session cookie.

verified.exploit_entry_point: AsyncHttpClient public library API. A request is built with setHeader/addHeader("Cookie", ...) and executed through AsyncHttpClient.executeRequest against a running HTTP server, on a client whose active (default) cookie store already holds a cookie for the origin (seeded here by a prior Set-Cookie response). The request serialised onto the wire carries the stored cookie instead of the caller's header. Reproduced against a loopback HTTP stub started inside the test process; no real network is used.
variants: First request, caller 'Cookie: SID=userB' vs same-name stored cookie SID=storeval: the serialised Cookie header is replaced by the stored value (request-serialisation path).
First request, caller 'Cookie: session=mine' vs a different-name stored cookie: the caller's cookie is dropped entirely from the serialised header (request-serialisation path, distinct assertion).
First request with two separate caller Cookie headers (a=1 and b=2) plus a stored cookie: both caller cookies are replaced by the store's single cookie (multi-header folding path).
Automatic redirect follow-up to the same origin (redirect-interceptor rebuild path): the continued request carries the stored cookie, not the caller's header.
Automatic retry after a 401 authentication challenge (auth-retry rebuild path): the retried, authenticated request carries the stored cookie, not the caller's header.
verified.project_tests_run: NOT RUN. The project's own tests for this area (AuthRetryCookieTest, RedirectCookieRotationTest) extend a Jetty-based harness and the surrounding suite pulls Jetty/Tomcat/Kerberos test dependencies; building that test tree offline was out of scope for a lean image. Instead the flaw was reproduced and the fix confirmed through the library's public API with standalone JUnit 5 tests driving a loopback HTTP stub, which exercise the same first-request, redirect and auth-retry code paths.

notes: Oracle (3-file upstream source fix): security 5/5, functional 6/6, reward 1.0. Vulnerable: security 0/5 (all exploits succeed), functional 6/6. fix_hops_only (CallerCookies+Redirect only, leaves the first-request serialiser unpatched): security 2/5, functional 6/6 -> security_fail. fix_serialiser_only (serialiser merge only, no hop reconciliation): security 5/5 but functional 4/6 (a server-rotated session is overridden by the stale caller header across a redirect and an auth retry) -> functional_fail. alt_correct_fix (independent serialiser merge via ServerCookieDecoder, same hop reconciliation): reward 1.0 -> pass, proving the tests do not hard-code the upstream patch shape.
